title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program Documentation Standard: Documented CGM Model Changes and Overlapping Sensor Supply
content:
# Documented change of CGM model and overlapping sensor supply

Documentation and Prior-Authorization Unit Standard, Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program.

This standard states when a documented change of CGM model leads the payer to be expected to pay for 30-day blocks of a new delivery of the CGM supply allowance (A4239) that overlap the latest refill's paid supply, so that those blocks come off the blocks at risk when Larkfield counts the units a plan member waiver covers on a Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program enrollment. It reads the over-limit justification (the latest medical record on the CGM program with purpose over-limit justification, a clinical document received to justify a quantity above the allowance, dated by the practitioner visit it records), the latest refill shipment of the CGM supply allowance, and the customer's Insulin Pump Program enrollment: its status and the pump delivery date recorded on it.

## The standard

The documented-change adjustment takes at-risk blocks off, by these rules:

1. When the customer's Insulin Pump Program is not closed, the pump delivery falls after the latest refill shipped and the over-limit justification is dated on or after the pump delivery, up to the first two at-risk blocks come off, the payer being expected to pay them as the transition to the model the pump requires, the superseded supply being unusable with the new pump.
2. When the over-limit justification is dated after the latest refill shipped and the pump delivery does not fall after it, the first at-risk block comes off, the documented clinical change being expected to be paid for it only, since the superseded supply can still be used.
3. Otherwise no block comes off.

Under rule 1 the blocks that come off are the first two at-risk blocks, or the only one where a single block is at risk; under rule 2 the block that comes off is the first at-risk block. A block that comes off is no longer counted at risk. An Insulin Pump Program enrollment that is referral received, pending authorization, active or on hold is not closed; a customer with no Insulin Pump Program enrollment has no pump delivery, so the pump delivery does not fall after the latest refill.

## Truth table

| Pump program not closed | Pump delivery after the latest refill shipped | Justification dated | Blocks that come off |
|---|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | on or after the pump delivery date | up to the first two at-risk blocks |
| yes | yes | before the pump delivery date, or none on record | none |
| no (closed) | yes | any date | none |
| any, or no pump program | no | after the latest refill's ship date | the first at-risk block |
| any, or no pump program | no | on or before the latest refill's ship date, or none on record | none |

## Cases (hypothetical dates)

- Latest refill shipped 1 April; an open Insulin Pump Program shows a pump delivered 20 April; a justification visit dated 20 April. The visit is on the delivery date, so up to two at-risk blocks come off. With three at-risk blocks, two come off and one remains at risk.
- Same refill and pump, justification visit dated 15 April: rule 1 fails, and rule 2 fails because the pump delivery falls after the refill. No block comes off.
- Latest refill shipped 1 April, no pump delivered after it, justification visit dated 2 April: the first at-risk block comes off. Dated 1 April, the same day the refill shipped, it is not after the refill and no block comes off.
